title: Add the quality selector for livestreams

timeline.body: #### What is it? - [x] Feature (user facing) #### Description of the changes in your PR This PR adds the ability to control the quality played for livestreams in NewPipe, both on main and popup players. The livestream quality selector uses the same popup menu as the quality selector for video streams. The resolution limit on mobile data on livestreams also now works with this PR (even if you need to reload the livestream if you started to play it on Wifi and then you switched to mobile data) with the `Auto` option. You can still choose an higher resolution than the limit you set in `Video and audio` settings, like for videos. Without setting a limit on mobile data or when playing a livestream on Wifi, the `Auto` option does the same thing as the current behavior (the quality played is managed by ExoPlayer and is, most of times, the highest available). However, the default video resolution on popup player and main player settings are not working. I don't really know how to do this and I don't really have the time to do it. #### Before/After Screenshots/Screen Record - Before: - After: #### Fixes the following issue(s) - Fixes #1239 #### APK testing The APK can be found by going to the "Checks" tab below the title. On the left pane, click on "CI", scroll down to "artifacts" and click "app" to download the zip file which contains the debug APK of this PR. #### Due diligence - [x] I read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Mmmh, by looking at the code above it seems like `StreamInfo` will be of livestream type only when `maybeBuildLiveMediaSource` fails (which should not happen for livestreams, unless `getHlsUrl` or `getDashMpdUrl` return empty urls) (`VideoPlaybackResolver` is the only place where `getDefaultResolutionIndex` and `getOverrideResolutionIndex` are *used*). So having `if (StreamTypeUtil.isLiveStream(streamInfo.getStreamType())) { return -1; }` in the player above is useless, I think (that's the only place where `getDefaultResolutionIndex` and `getOverrideResolutionIndex` are *overridden*).

reply.body: Not sure about that, I'd like to hear advice of other team members.
Well, let's keep it and just add a comment explaining that `return -1` should be unreachable (explaining why)

> So having `if (StreamTypeUtil.isLiveStream(streamInfo.getStreamType())) { return -1; }` in the player above is useless

Indeed, I just look better at the code and you are right, that's useless to set `-1` and this can even create bugs because no video source would be available for livestreams (because `MediaSourceTag.getSelectedVideoStream()` will return `null`).

So I will rollback my changes here and keep code as it was before.

When I worked on this PR first, I tried to set the quality played based on user settings and not to limit the maximum resolution which can be played.

But it wasn't working because the playback wasn't intialized when the setting of my selection override was called (so the currentMappedTrackInfo was null) so I was not able to set the selection override.

Is there any way to do what I said instead of the current behavior (which is setting the maximum resolution allowed)?

@Redirion I think you are the best to know how to do this, that's why I am asking for your help.
If it wasn't clear I meant here ...
... and here in my comment in the other review
Please use a shorter name (e.g. `updateQualityForLivestreamsIfNeeded`), the Javadoc explains the rest

This is being done independently of from where the function returns, so it should not be duplicated, but should just be put below `if (isDefaultResolutionOverrideOrMaxVideoSizeAndFrameRateSet) { return; }`
@litetex is right, this can be put at the bottom of the function just before `return true` since it is called always.

Also here, maybe use `isUsingDefaultResolutionForLivestreams` which is shorter and more meaningful. I can't understand what `isDefaultResolutionOverrideOrMaxVideoSizeAndFrameRateSet` means, I just see that it is only used inside `setDefaultResolutionForLivestreams` and it prevents that function from being executed multiple times
Marking as draft because it seems the quality selected automatically is not updated in the quality selected textview.
tested it, seems to work just fine (default quality selection, manual quality selection)

Add the quality selector for livestreams

timeline.message:
Allow users to see if the quality used is selected by ExoPlayer or by themselves

If the quality is selected by ExoPlayer, the app will show Auto (QUALITY) where QUALITY is the height of the stream + "p" + the frame rate of the stream if its value is more than 30.
In order to show this, a string with two placeholders has been created: %1$s represents the Auto string and %2$s the resolution or the bandwidth.
Otherwise, only QUALITY is shown.
Also fixes an issue when stream's height is not available (the bitrate of the stream was shown without the "bps" string).

timeline.body: Almost ready to merge in my opinion, just a couple of questions

> It seems there are better ways to do quality selection when initializing the playback, by using a CustomTrackSelector.
> It seems to be quite complex 

Could you elaborate on what you mean by better ways? I'm not too familiar with TrackSelector but complexity is exactly the reason why, during latest ExoPlayer upgrade, I chose to go back and use `DefaultTrackSelector` instead of whipping out another hacky implementation of `CustomTrackSelector`. Don't really have the time to work on this now unfortunately, but I'd avoid extending the default track selector if possible, unless there is a real need to do so.

> the current way used in this PR to select/override tracks is now deprecated 

Exo devs will eventually have to update [their demo track selector](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/release-v2/demos/main/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/demo/TrackSelectionDialog.java) that we can use as reference.

@TiA4f8R ping for https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/pull/7260#issuecomment-1107659048 and https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/pull/7260#discussion_r808523567 (but I understand this PR will have to wait for changes on exoplayer's end)

Closing this PR, as it is quite old and its code is now using deprecated features in ExoPlayer. It also seems very hard to rebase it on top of the `dev` branch.

I found easier ways to do parts of the feature, starting again almost from scratch. I will open a new PR including the addition of the feature and some fixes/improvements in the player (mostly related to the `SourceType` of sources, which are needed to do properly this feature) soon.
